text: TEL AVIS - More than 40 Israeli businesses attended a business networking workshop in Tel Aviv on November 16 to seek Vietnamese suppliers and explore new business opportunities.

The event was jointly organised by the Vietnam Trade Office in Israel and the Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce (FICC), bringing together companies involved in importing goods and exporting equipment and technologies.

Speaking at the workshop, Ksenia Koroleva, Head of International Cooperation at FICC, said the event offered Israeli importers an opportunity to expand partnerships and seek overseas sources of supply, with Việt Nam regarded as an important sourcing market.
It also laid the groundwork for stronger cooperation between FICC and the Vietnam Trade Office in 2027, she added.

Lê Thái Hòa, Trade Counsellor at the Vietnamese Embassy in Israel and head of the Trade Office, outlined key provisions of the Vietnam-Israel Free Trade Agreement (VIFTA) and the opportunities it has generated after nearly two years of implementation.

Amid disruptions to supply chains in Israel caused by the ongoing conflict, more Israeli businesses are seeking new suppliers and partners, particularly for products in which Việt Nam has strong export capabilities, he said.
At the business-matching session, Israeli importers and distribution representatives expressed interest in securing stable, large-volume supplies from Việt Nam.

Their needs cover food and processed food, agricultural products, confectionery, consumer goods, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, household products, tyres, construction materials, electronics and office equipment.
The Vietnam Trade Office provided market information and helped connect Israeli importers with suitable Vietnamese businesses, manufacturers and exporters.

It also introduced a number of trade fairs and specialised exhibitions scheduled to take place in Việt Nam in 2027, encouraging Israeli companies to attend to explore the market and establish direct partnerships.
According to statistics cited at the event, two-way trade between Việt Nam and Israel reached nearly US$3.5 billion in the first 10 months of 2026, up 12.7 per cent year on year.
Việt Nam 's exports to Israel totalled $997.1 million, surging 41.4 per cent.
If market conditions remain stable, bilateral trade is projected to reach around $4.4 billion for the whole year, with Việt Nam 's exports estimated at about $1.3 billion.
The workshop is expected to strengthen business links, broaden market access and support further growth in Vietnamese exports to Israel. - VNA/VNS
